notes: 'neither' is read as a fusion of the second גַּם with the לֹא of the same clause (rule 35); the competing reading gives 'neither' to גַּם alone and marks לֹא unrepresented, but the English word carries the negation as well as the addition.
'could' is given to יָדָעוּ, whose 'know how to' sense the ASV renders modally; 'blush' remains the infinitive's.

The 'that' of 'at the time that I visit them' is added: עֵת is written as the antecedent and a finite clause is juxtaposed to it with no relative morpheme, which rule 46's rider sends to rules 30 and 55.
